definitions.explanation: The state of flowers being fully open. Most commonly associated with cherry blossoms, but applies to any flowering plant.

examples.japanese: {桜|さくら}が{満開|まんかい}だ。
examples.english: The cherry blossoms are in full bloom.

examples.japanese: {公園|こうえん}の{梅|うめ}が{満開|まんかい}を{迎|むか}えた。
examples.english: The plum trees in the park have reached full bloom.

examples.japanese: {今年|ことし}は{例年|れいねん}より{早|はや}く{桜|さくら}が{満開|まんかい}になった。
examples.english: This year the cherry blossoms reached full bloom earlier than usual.

notes:
USAGE:
Used predicatively as {満開|まんかい}だ or with になる to indicate reaching full bloom. A key term during cherry blossom season, when weather forecasts track {開花|かいか} (first bloom) and {満開|まんかい} (full bloom) dates across the country.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {満開|まんかい}になる: to reach full bloom
- {満開|まんかい}を{迎|むか}える: to reach full bloom
- {満開|まんかい}の{桜|さくら}: cherry blossoms in full bloom
- {満開|まんかい}{予想|よそう}: full bloom forecast
